newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Tapie may face heavier jail term.
newsitem.headline: France's Tapie may face heavier jail term.

text.p: A French public prosecutor urged an appeals court on Thursday to sentence fallen tycoon Bernard Tapie to eight months in jail and 16 months suspended for fraud in managing his luxury yacht.
At his earlier trial, the flamboyant former minister was given a 30-month suspended sentence and banned from managing companies on charges of misappropriation of company funds and bankruptcy.
Public prosecutor Daniel Fortin urged the court to impose a heavier punishment on Tapie for tax evasion linked to the yacht, asking for the term to be raised to eight months from six months.
A court had convicted him for passing off the majestic 74-metre (245-foot), four-masted Phocea as a means of promoting his business although he was its only beneficiary.
Tapie is already serving a separate eight-month jail term for rigging a soccer match.

He vigorously defended himself against fraud charges. "I am not saying we were not at fault. But to come and tell me that all this was Machiavellian and calculated is total stupidity," he told the court.

Tapie, 54, has tumbled from political and business stardom since 1993, when he rigged a league match to give his team Marseille an easy game before their successful European Cup final against AC Milan.
The $11 million yacht, which at the height of Tapie's wealth and fame was moored proudly in the old port of Marseille, has been seized and is on sale.
